object_description: two buildings of different sizes set transversely to the slope defining a shared outdoor space
design_condition: the two volumes take up the settlement structure west of the castle and reach into the open landscape chamber, positioned transversely to the slope so that they define a shared outdoor space connected to the historic complex

positive: The arrival situation is clarified and characteristic outdoor spaces bring the new ensemble together with the historic complex
The two volumes take up the settlement structure west of the castle and reach into the open landscape chamber
Positioned transversely to the slope they define an outdoor space convincingly connected to the existing complex
A path connection creates permeability to the buildings to the south
The shared outdoor space gives the ensemble an identity and relates it to the monastery garden
Access to gymnasium and school is logically from the shared outdoor space
The gymnasium entrance with foyer at the end of the square is spatially convincing
Social activities close to hall and foyer can take place on the square outside school hours
The organisation of the basic level with covered outdoor area and central open hall promotes community and communication
The split-level typology enables good orientation and forms an interesting sequence of rooms
The basic rooms each have group and therapy rooms with a connection to the landscape
Removing the gymnasium in the valley allows an outdoor pool usable independently of the school
The all-weather pitch is clearly assigned to the pool and the checkroom building
The courtyard is given a comprehensible design with fountain, hedges and continuous paving
The position of the new buildings creates a nice connection and an appealing arrival point as a social meeting place
Despite the split into two buildings a relatively good compactness is achieved
The grey energy requirement is achieved without any problems
The skeleton construction allows a certain flexibility of use
Small floor area, medium compactness and simple construction result in an economical solution
negative: Turning the basic level volume west diminishes the relationship of the playground to the landscape
The foyer with its narrow staircase appears too small and lacks spaciousness
Access to the basic level is awkward with a ramp
The visual relationship to the outdoor spaces of the base rooms is only partially guaranteed
The internal and external appearance is not very coherent
The facade expression appears alien in this location despite the intended village reference
Whether trees could be placed above the archaeological finds remains questionable
The recessed entrance to the school is not very attractive
The position of the houses on the upper level tends to turn away from the landscape and is difficult to understand
The narrow space between the buildings at the lower level is not very attractive and questionable as a school outdoor area
It is not directly visible from all classrooms and the upper classrooms lack directly accessible outdoor spaces
The network of paths is too dense
The glass parts shaded by the sheds provide reduced daylight and hardly any passive solar use
The daylight quotient in the gymnasium is likely to be achieved only with difficulty
Most of the plywood facade is unprotected, so faster ageing is expected
The positioning and extension of the gymnasium far into the landscape is not convincing
The rotation of the basic level appears random
